Current behaviour: Collects card number, expiry and CVC then fakes a 900ms delay and generates the paid reference client-side. Nothing is charged and nothing is stored; submitForm is imported at :7 but never called
What it needs: Real payment capture, a persisted booking record, and a confirmation email triggered by the payment actually succeeding
Suggested API / service: Stripe — Payment Intents + Stripe Elements (raw card number never touches our server) or Stripe Checkout redirect for the fastest PCI-SAQ-A path. Booking store: Supabase/Postgres table, or Cal.com / Google Calendar API for the slot. Webhook payment_intent.succeeded -> write booking -> send confirmation via Resend

Current behaviour: Client-side lookup against public/installation/au-postcodes.json (2765 rows). Works, but the supported flags are unverified and the file is publicly fetchable
What it needs: The real serviced-postcode list. No API required — this is a data problem, not a wiring problem
Suggested API / service: None needed. Optionally move the lookup behind a route handler so the flags are not a public static file. Data pending IT per docs/content-sources/general.txt

What it needs: Nothing new to build; only the shared hardening in FB-07/FB-08

Current behaviour: Works — emails support with a single file attachment (the receipt). Nothing is stored, so a registration cannot be looked up later
What it needs: Persistence. A registration that only exists as an email cannot be queried when a warranty claim arrives
Suggested API / service: Supabase/Postgres table (or Airtable for a no-code start) keyed on serial number + purchase date. Keep the Resend email as the notification, add the row as the record

Current behaviour: Emails support, but evidence photos are sent as FILENAMES ONLY — evidence.map(f => f.name).join(). The API's single attachment slot is taken by the receipt, so support receives no images
What it needs: Real multi-file upload, and a link from the claim to the customer's registration
Suggested API / service: Vercel Blob or UploadThing / S3 presigned URLs for the photos, then email the links via Resend. Same datastore as FB-04 so a claim resolves against a registration
